pool_nohuge.meaning: A has no pool THP exclusion (no consumer in the fork); B maps the 32 GiB pool with MADV_NOHUGEPAGE

spill_flag.meaning: no spill tier in A (flag absent), tier present and off in B

B.label: promoted port + pool MADV_NOHUGEPAGE + port server

claim.confirm_when: NOT SUPPORTED at n=2/arm (no interval reaches 90 %); a follow-up window at n>=3 confirms only when its 90 % interval excludes 0 AND exceeds the pre-registered delta

delta_pre_registered.short_pp_read_tps: from the W2 pilot (per shape, frozen before the claim legs)

claim.follow_up: any claim (confirm, no difference, within delta) requires a FOLLOW-UP window at n>=3 per arm; this window's records are that window's baseline and are descriptive only
claim.level_note: the level applies to a FOLLOW-UP window at n>=3 only; at n=2/arm the minimum exact two-sided p is 0.33, so no 90 % (or 95 %) interval exists
claim.method: exact / Hodges-Lehmann two-sided interval at n>=3 per arm for a follow-up window (3v3 gives C(6,3)=20 allocations, minimum exact p = 0.10). This window is n=2/arm: 2v2 gives C(4,2)=6 allocations, minimum exact two-sided p = 0.33, and the outputs are DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY
outputs: descriptive: per-leg rates, full ranges, memory beside speed
claim.report: median + full range, speed beside memory, boot-state confounds named, every comparison labelled descriptive-only
claim.within_delta_clause: NOT SUPPORTED at n=2/arm. In a FOLLOW-UP window at n>=3 'within +/-delta' is licensed ONLY when the entire 90% interval lies inside +/-delta; a wide interval straddling the delta boundary is INDETERMINATE, not 'within 5%'

could_not_build: No boot, no leg and no measurement was run: the fixer lane is CPU-only, prod is serving, and the windows are operator-gated.

The 2x2 verdicts are STATIC (binary literal scan + server argv model). The servers' drafting chooser was not executed; its no-op outcome for these names is asserted from the regex in both trees and must be confirmed from the first boot line.
W4's optional third boot per cell (min p 0.10) is planned but not prepared; 2 boots per cell is what the budget covers.
The W2 pilot deltas are not filled yet: the pilot boots must run first, then port_ab_legs.py --freeze-pilot W2 writes them here. Claim legs refuse until then.
The helper fill band is derived from the 7,000 MiB cap and the Phase-1 row size, not measured under this tuple; the first boot's fill is recorded and checked against it.
deviations: The arms cannot be byte-identical: arm B carries --conversation-spill-mib 0 and arm A has no such option. That is the declared structural difference, not a lever.

model_name is matched to 'ud-iq3_xxs' and reasoning_budget_tokens to 0: the adopted bases served different values (A 55,000 / B 2,000 and two names); neither name matches a drafter regex in either server, so drafting.apply leaves the args untouched.
A base's --conversation-cache-dir pointed into the helper-ipc worktree; both arms now use a fresh per-boot directory under the harness tree.
The boot key includes the boot group (W2-A-dec-r1 / W2-A-sht-r1): W2's two boot shapes must never share a cache dir, sockets, logs or state file.
The helper's environment is frozen (PATH/HOME/TERM/STRATA_HELPER_REPLY_TIMEOUT_MS) and recorded per boot, instead of inheriting the caller's shell.

W2 now has a discarded decode warmup boot per arm as W1/W3 do, and the budgets count every discarded boot; the contract's numbers (1.5-2.5 h W1, 1.2-2 h W3) are kept beside the derived planning ranges.

helper_fill_band.basis: fill-mib 7000 binds at ~6.84 GiB; Phase-1 row size 1.87-1.92 MiB/row -> 3,646-3,743 rows; rows allow 6 % either side, GiB is 6.55-6.90 (the upper bound is 66 MiB over the 7,000 MiB cap, for the helper's startup accounting); checked per boot, never widened

frozen_tuple.helper_fill_note: fill-mib 7000 caps both helpers below the 7.09/7.34 GiB fills the Phase-1 record lists; the band above is what the boot lines are checked against, and it is never widened after the fact
